route: Work Permit (Immigration Act, s. 17; Ministry of National Security)

permit.applies: The employer applies through the Ministry of National Security, for a specialised position, while the worker resides outside the Federation
permit.first: The position advertised in the local media for three consecutive weeks, consultation with the Labour Department and evidence of trying to fill it locally; the Immigration Regulations (reg. 22, S.R.O. 33/1991) ask the job to be advertised in a local newspaper and on local radio for at least one month, the employer to be registered with Social Security and hold a Business and Occupations Licence, and a visitor to leave and re-enter after the permit is approved.

fees.what: Work permit, entertainers (1 to 4 persons), each
Work permit, entertainers (5 or more persons)
Work permit for one month or less
Temporary permit, each additional month (not exceeding two months)
Work permit for a calendar year
Variation or replacement of a work permit

permit.feesNote: Immigration Regulations reg. 23 (substituted by S.R.O. 13/1997), as printed in the Revised Laws to 31 December 2020; the employer pays and may not deduct it from the worker's pay.
permit.validityNote: Fees are set for a calendar year, for a month or less, and for temporary permits of up to two further months; renewal should be sought at least three months before expiry, and the worker leaves when it isn't renewed.
permit.exemptNote: None for a foreign performer: only citizens, approved CARICOM citizens and citizens of an OECS Protocol Member State work without the permit (Immigration Act s. 19(1)); entertainers pay their own permit fee (reg. 23).

sources.title: SKNIS, Ministry of National Security reminds employers of work permit procedures (28 September 2020)
sources.said: As per Section 17 of the Immigration Act, an application for a work permit can only be made for a specialized position while the applicant resides outside of the Federation of St. Kitts and Nevis. … The position must first be advertised in the local media for three consecutive weeks. Additionally, the employer must also show that they have consulted with the Labour Department and provide evidence of trying to fill the vacant post locally. … Request for renewal of a work permit must be made no later than two weeks before the expiration of the current work permit.

sources.title: Law Commission of St Kitts and Nevis, Immigration Act Cap. 6.02 with its regulations (Revised Laws to 31 December 2020), regs. 22-23
sources.said: an application for a Work Permit shall be made by the prospective employer on behalf of the prospective employee; … he or she shall advertise the job in a local newspaper and over the local Radio Station for a period of at least one month … such renewal should be sought at least three months prior to the expiration of such Work Permit; … (a) For a calendar year $ 1,600.00 (b) For a period of one month or less $ 250.00 (c) Temporary permits for each additional month not exceeding two months $ 250.00 (d) Entertainers(5 or more persons) $ 900.00 (e) Entertainers (1 to 4 persons) $ 175.00 each (f) For variation or replacement of a Work Permit $ 25.00

sources.title: Law Commission of St Kitts and Nevis, Immigration Act Cap. 6.02 (Revision Date 31 Dec 2020), s. 19 and Second Schedule, with the Immigration Regulations reg. 23 (saved l4w/files/p1c/KN-act.pdf)
sources.said: 19. (1) A person, other than a citizen, an approved CARICOM citizen or a citizen of a Protocol Member State, shall not, while in Saint Christopher and Nevis, engage in any occupation or accept employment without having first obtained a written permit granted by the Minister for that purpose. … (4) An applicant for a work permit shall make the application while the prospective employee is outside of the Federation, except that this provision shall not apply in respect of an application for renewal of a work permit or any other case as the Minister may, by Order, direct. … SECOND SCHEDULE PERMITTED ENTRANTS … PART II … 5. Persons entering Saint Christopher and Nevis for the purpose of engaging in sport, dramatic, artistic or other cultural activities. … 23. The fee for the issue of Work Permits shall be as follows— … (d) Entertainers(5 or more persons) $ 900.00 (e) Entertainers (1 to 4 persons) $ 175.00 each
